entry.title: Localizing Open-Source ERP: How Odoo 19 is Adapted for Solar Hijri, Complex Tax, and RTL
entry.summary: Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) adoption in non-Western markets frequently faces a severe bottleneck: native ERP engines are deeply hardcoded around the Gregorian calendar, Latin typography, and Western accounting conventions. In countries like Iran and Afghanistan, where official business records strictly require the Solar Hijri (Jalali / Shamsi) calendar and right-to-left (RTL) localization, running a standard ERP implementation often turns into an engineering nightmare. Historically, localization teams made the fatal mistake of forking the upstream source code or creating parallel database engines. When upstream releases a major version (e.g., Odoo 17 to Odoo 18, and now Odoo 19), forked implementations break catastrophically. The engineering team at Abrak Cloud ERP pioneered an alternative architectural approach: pure non-destructive extension (_inherit). By implementing dual-layer conversion adapters, the database persists dates in standard UTC ISO format, while the web client (OWL/JavaScript) and report rendering engines translate date projections on the fly using high-precision algorithms. Precision Solar Hijri Engine: Full leap-year precision conforming to the 33-year astronomical cycle, available via the Jalali Calendar Odoo 19 framework. Direct Electronic Invoicing & Cryptographic Compliance: Automated generation of 22-digit cryptographic tax identifiers, canonical JSON payload assembly, and asymmetric RSA/ECC signing for national tax authority gateways. Dedicated Database Isolation: Ensuring each enterprise tenant operates within an independent PostgreSQL database container, eliminating data co-mingling risks found in shared-tenant SaaS architectures. Developers and international engineering teams interested in modern open-source enterprise software architecture can explore the comprehensive documentation and live sandboxes at abrak.org.

entry.title: Whisper Hallucinations: 'Thanks for Watching' in 9% of My Transcripts
entry.summary: A user emailed me a screenshot of their feedback report. Under "Communication," my scoring model had written: "Closed the answer with 'Thanks for watching,' which feels scripted and out of place in a live conversation." They never said it. They paused for about four seconds, decided they were done, and stopped talking. Whisper filled the silence for them, and then an LLM graded them on the words Whisper made up. This post covers Whisper hallucinations on silence: how often they happened in my pipeline (9.2% of clips), why the built-in no_speech_threshold didn't catch them, and the config change that got the count from 183 to 4.
